title: Cleopatra: Ms. Understood
summary: Josh and Chuck profile Cleopatra VII, the last ruling pharaoh of Ptolemaic Egypt, covering her accession alongside her brother, her alliances with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony, the Roman propaganda that shaped her image, and her death in 30 BC. The episode also includes tour announcements at the start and a listener mail segment honoring a ten-year-old named Zach at the end.

segments.title: Tour dates and opening banter
segments.summary: Josh announces Stuff You Should Know Live tour dates in Chicago, Toronto, Boston, Portland Maine, Florida, New Orleans and Brooklyn, then the hosts tease the confusing Roman-numeral names in the Cleopatra story.

segments.title: Cleopatra's historical reputation and sources
segments.summary: The hosts explain that little is documented about Cleopatra by Egyptians, that most sources are Greco-Roman, and that Plutarch was among the first to show sympathy. Romans portrayed her through sex and magic because she threatened patriarchal rule.

segments.title: The Ptolemaic dynasty and Cleopatra's background
segments.summary: Ptolemy I, a Macedonian general, took Egypt after Alexander's death and founded the Ptolemaic line, which ruled for a few hundred years. Cleopatra's ethnicity is uncertain. She spoke Egyptian, observed Egyptian customs and used multiple languages in diplomacy, which diminished her officials' power.

segments.title: Ascension to the throne and Egypt's situation
segments.summary: Cleopatra took the throne at eighteen with her ten-year-old brother as co-ruler, under a tradition requiring a male consort. Egypt faced floods, famine and a weak economy, and her father had mortgaged the country to Rome, making Egypt a client state.

segments.title: Roman civil war and Pompey's death
segments.summary: Rome was split by the triumvirate of Caesar, Pompey and Crassus. Caesar crossed the Rubicon and defeated Pompey, who fled to Egypt, where Ptolemy XIII had him killed to win Caesar's favor.

segments.title: The carpet entrance and Caesar's alliance
segments.summary: Caesar arrived in Egypt and declared martial law. Cleopatra reportedly smuggled herself past the lines rolled in a carpet to meet him, and won his support. Ptolemy XIII drowned fleeing, and Arsinoe was paraded in chains and exiled to the Temple of Artemis at Ephesus.

segments.title: Caesarion and Cleopatra's rule in Rome
segments.summary: Cleopatra bore Caesar a son, Caesarion, whom Caesar acknowledged but did not name as heir. Cleopatra stayed in Rome across the river from Caesar's house. The hosts describe her as beloved by Egyptians, her patriotic image, and her expansion of trade, including a tax break for a Roman general and her handwritten decree.

segments.title: Caesar's death and the second triumvirate
segments.summary: After Caesar was murdered, Octavian and Mark Antony allied against Brutus and Cassius. Lepidus joined as the third member of the second triumvirate. Antony and Octavian defeated Brutus and Cassius at the Battle of Philippi, and Antony gained control of the East including Egypt.

segments.title: Meeting Mark Antony at Tarsus
segments.summary: Cleopatra refused to be summoned and later arrived at Tarsus on a lavish barge styled as Aphrodite. Antony dined with her and they formed a relationship, with three children together. They drank together in the Inimitable Livers club, and she dissolved a pearl in vinegar to show her wealth.

segments.title: Antony's land grants and Octavian's propaganda
segments.summary: Antony gave land to Cleopatra's children, angering Octavian. Octavian ran a propaganda campaign portraying Cleopatra as a foreign temptress and threat to Rome, and the Senate stripped Antony of his titles, leading to war.

segments.title: Death of Antony and Cleopatra
segments.summary: During the siege, Antony took his own life after believing Cleopatra was dead, and died in her arms. Octavian planned to parade Cleopatra in Rome as a captive, so she took her own life with poison on August 12, 30 BC, with two servants. Theories about the poison include a cobra bite and an arrangement with Octavian.

segments.title: Legacy, image and the naming of August
segments.summary: Cleopatra was buried beside Antony. The hosts discuss how Roman biographers shaped her image, her looks and the enduring focus on her beauty. Octavian took the name Augustus, which the hosts connect to the month of August.

segments.title: Listener mail for Zach's tenth birthday
segments.summary: Listener Mandy writes that her stepson Zach, who has ADHD and loves the show on car rides, is turning ten, and asks for a birthday shout-out. The hosts wish him a happy birthday.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts encourage listeners to read more about Cleopatra, mention how to contact the show by email, and sign off.
